**If you're diagnosing a `harness_shared.test_runs` row whose named failing
test(s) don't exist in the commit it's stamped with (`git show <sha>:<file> |
grep <test name>` comes back empty at that sha AND its neighbors), suspect a
torn read from the harness-scoped ad-hoc runner before you suspect the ledger
itself is corrupt** — this is a known, fixed-at-the-source class of
misattribution, distinct from
[gate-red-on-quarantined-file-phantom-attribution](/internal/docs/agent-insights/gate-red-on-quarantined-file-phantom-attribution)
(that one is a log-parsing bug in the isolated green-checkpoint run; this one
is a genuine torn read against the live shared tree).

## The signature (incident 2026-07-27, EI-18795303393201472)

A `test_runs` row (`status='fail'`, `source` from the harness Tests-tab path)
named test cases that exist in NO commit near its stamped `commit_sha` — only
in a LATER commit, once the author's edit (which was mid-flight when the run
executed) finished landing. `git log`/mtimes showed: the test file was written
to the tree, the ad-hoc run executed a few seconds later (before the matching
implementation was written), and the implementation landed after that. The run
observed a state that was never a commit and never will be.

## Root cause

`POST /harness/:slug/testing/run` (`endpoint-route/routes/harness/testing.ts`,
backing the `testing:run` MCP tool) runs `npx vitest run <files>`
**synchronously, `cwd: root`, against the shared, concurrently-edited working
tree** — not an isolated checkout (unlike the actual green-checkpoint gate,
which per its own header comment always judges a dedicated isolated worktree).
It then called `git rev-parse HEAD` to stamp `commit_sha` **after the run
finished**. Between the run starting and that sample, a peer's edit or a
git-sync commit can change what's on disk, so the stamped sha can name a
commit whose real content never matches what vitest actually executed.

This matters beyond a single false-attribution report:
`ledgerFilesForCandidate` / `verifyGateVerdict` (`why-chain.ts`,
WI-4533/EI-17603) treat `test_runs` rows matched by `commit_sha` as
**first-hand evidence** to cross-check the release gate's own named failures
for the EXACT candidate under verdict. A torn-read row can poison that very
cross-check for an unrelated commit that happens to share the stamp.

## The fix (migration 709)

The runner now snapshots `{ commit, git status --porcelain -- <files> }`
**both before and after** the vitest run (`computeWorktreeDirty` in
`testing-run-store.ts`). Any mismatch — HEAD moved, or the tested files carry
uncommitted changes at either snapshot, or either git read failed
(fail-safe: unreadable ⇒ treated as dirty) — marks the row
`worktree_dirty = true`. `ledgerFilesForCandidate` excludes dirty rows from
its commit-scoped first-hand-evidence query (`AND worktree_dirty = false`);
the time-windowed proxy `recentFailingFiles` deliberately keeps them, since
"something failed recently, somewhere" doesn't depend on sha precision.

Not yet covered by the same fix (filed as follow-up, same failure class):
`testing-run-store.ts`'s `persistFallbackRow` (the node/shell admin-suite
fallback path) and the in-process vitest reporter used by admin-ui spawns
both sample git context after their run finishes too — lower blast radius
(their commit_sha isn't the primary input to `ledgerFilesForCandidate`'s
gate cross-check today) but the same hazard shape.
